name: New York City
operatingHours: Subway runs 24 hours a day, 7 days a week — the only system here with no overnight closure.
fareInfo: NYC Subway is a flat $3.00 per ride via OMNY contactless, regardless of distance — the same price for one stop or the length of the city. Weekly cap: $35, after which further rides that week are free.

lines.name: N/Q/R/W
lines.firstLast: Runs 24/7 like the rest of the NYC subway — no first/last train. Overnight (~midnight–5 AM) trains come every 20–30 min instead of every 5–10.

lines.name: A/C/E
lines.firstLast: Runs 24/7 like the rest of the NYC subway — no first/last train. Overnight (~midnight–5 AM) trains come every 20–30 min instead of every 5–10.

sights.name: Central Park
sights.note: 843 acres in the heart of Manhattan, managed by the Central Park Conservancy since 1980.

sights.name: The Metropolitan Museum of Art
sights.note: NYC's most-visited museum — 5,000 years of art from around the world.

sights.name: The National 9/11 Memorial & Museum
sights.note: Twin reflecting pools and museum honoring the 2,983 lives lost.

sights.name: Empire State Building
sights.note: The 86th & 102nd floor observatories offer 360° views of Midtown.

sights.name: Top of the Rock
sights.note: 3-tiered observation deck on the 67th, 69th, and 70th floors of 30 Rockefeller Plaza.

sights.name: The High Line
sights.note: 1.5-mile elevated railway turned park, Hudson River & skyline views.

sights.name: Times Square
sights.note: Neon billboards, Broadway theaters — the crossroads of the world.

sights.name: Statue of Liberty
sights.note: Gift from France, 1886 — ferry required, book Ellis Island combo tickets ahead.

sights.name: Grand Central Terminal
sights.note: Opened 1913 — the celestial ceiling in the Main Concourse is NYC's most extraordinary public space.

sights.name: Brooklyn Bridge
sights.note: Opened 1883 — walk the pedestrian promenade between Manhattan and Brooklyn.

sights.name: American Museum of Natural History
sights.note: Dinosaur skeletons, the Hayden Planetarium, blue whale model.

sights.name: New York Public Library - Stephen A. Schwarzman Building
sights.note: Beaux-Arts main branch — the Rose Main Reading Room is a free must-see.
sights.hours: 10:00 AM–6:00 PM, till 8 PM Tue/Wed, closed Sun

sights.name: Chelsea Market
sights.note: Food hall in the Meatpacking District — dozens of vendors under one roof.

sights.name: Staten Island Ferry
sights.note: Free ferry with Statue of Liberty & skyline views — no ticket needed.

sights.name: Rockefeller Center
sights.note: Historic complex — Top of the Rock, NBC Studios, the famous ice rink in winter.

railStations.name: Penn Station
railStations.note: Amtrak, NJ Transit & LIRR hub beneath Madison Square Garden — also home to the newer Moynihan Train Hall.
railStations.hours: Station open 24 hours. Amtrak/NJ Transit/LIRR trains run all day with reduced overnight frequency — no single last train, check your specific route.

railStations.name: Grand Central Terminal
railStations.note: Metro-North commuter rail hub to Westchester, Connecticut & the Hudson Valley.
railStations.hours: Station open ~5:30 AM–2:00 AM. Metro-North trains run on individual branch timetables with a real overnight gap (~2–5 AM) — check MTA Metro-North for your line.

airports.name: John F. Kennedy International Airport
airports.transitNote: ~60 min to Manhattan via AirTrain JFK (shown on map, connects to A train at Howard Beach) — requires a transfer, not a one-seat ride
airports.hours: A train runs 24/7 — no first/last train. Overnight (~midnight–5 AM) trains every 20–30 min instead of every 5–10. Note: the AirTrain JFK connection itself costs a separate $8.50, on top of the $3.00 subway fare.

airports.name: LaGuardia Airport
airports.transitNote: No rail connection exists — LGA is the only major East Coast airport without one (the AirTrain project was cancelled in 2023). Q70 bus to Astoria-Ditmars Blvd (N/W train, shown on map) or M60 bus to Manhattan.

airports.name: Newark Liberty International Airport
airports.transitNote: ~30–45 min via AirTrain Newark to NJ Transit/Amtrak, then to Penn Station — not on the NYC Subway map shown
